findings.passage: It’s intended to make the process so difficult it prevents Coloradans from buying guns, and this is just the beginning.
findings.note: Guest column under her byline about SB 25-003, which requires a training and background-check process to buy certain semiautomatic guns. She describes the process as costly and unworkable, says it is meant to prevent purchases, and expects a further assault-weapons ban bill next session.

findings.passage: Though legislators labeled this bill as a “safety measure” to educate the public, it’s been such a hurdle only 14% of applicants have completed all requirements.
findings.note: In the same column she criticizes the permit and training requirement and the three-day wait under SB 25-003 as a hurdle to buying.

permit or training to buy a gun

findings.passage: The so-called 'assault weapons' ban bill is the most concerning, but they all have tragic consequences for law-abiding citizens. The ‘assault weapons’ bill is incredibly deceptive. They want to ban not only every kind of ‘scary’ gun like ARs and AKs, but also 80-90% of semi-automatic firearms popular today, including handguns and shotguns,
findings.note: Quoted by a national news outlet in 2024, before she held office, when she was a Colorado Springs gun-store owner. She opposes the 2024 assault-weapons ban bill and argues its feature list is cosmetic.
subjects: ban on assault-style guns

findings.passage: Twenty-nine states currently have constitutional carry. While over 50% of the country recognizes the Constitution, states like Colorado are going backwards,
findings.note: Quoted by a national news outlet in 2024 (before she held office). She cites permitless carry in other states and criticizes Colorado's existing gun laws, including universal background checks, magazine limits, safe storage and red-flag laws.
subjects: carry a gun without a permit

findings.passage: Colorado law currently allows for individual school districts to determine their own armed security protocols, something that is often utilized by charter schools and rural districts across the state,
findings.note: Quoted by a national news outlet in 2024 (before she held office) on HB 24-1310, which would end the exemption letting school staff carry on school grounds. She says she has certified school employees to carry and that response from the sheriff can be far away.
subjects: guns in schools and sensitive places

findings.passage: Most of these proposed bills in Colorado will hurt the underprivileged the most, ensuring only the wealthy can protect themselves or express their constitutionally protected right,
findings.note: Quoted by a national news outlet in 2024 (before she held office) on a proposed 11% tax on gun and ammunition sales and on liability insurance for gun owners (HB 24-1270). She says they add cost, calls the tax a "sin tax" and says self-defense is a human right.
